.qc-cache/coldwater-strict-2026-10-02-r15/rules/harbor-webdev-rubric-qc/references/staged-task-contract.md (task.toml block, budget nesting line 111, restart tool line 163)
evidence: NESTING (static, verified on these bytes). rewardkit runs with --max-concurrent-agent 1 (tests/test.sh:207), so judges in a suite run one after another and the sum must fit. Gates: gates/render/judge.toml:4 'timeout = 600' + gates/constraints/judge.toml:4 'timeout = 600' = 1200 < 'run_suite gates 1500' (test.sh:213), 300 s spare. Scored: functional 9000 (scored/functional/judge.toml:4) + polish 900 + visual 900 = 10800 < 'run_suite scored 11100' (test.sh:224), 300 s spare. Verifier: 1500 + 11100 = 12600 < task.toml:27 'timeout_sec = 13200.0', 600 s spare, which covers the pre-suite work (file copy, liveness loop of 120 x 0.25 s = 30 s nominal at test.sh:116-121, prompt substitution, two score.py calls). 13200 s = 3 h 40 min, below the five-hour limit. Restart: the helper's own readiness loop is 30 s plus up to 5 s kill wait (test.sh:160-176), inside restart_mcp.py:11 'HELPER_TIMEOUT_SEC = 55'. Every one of these values, and test.sh itself, is identical to the frozen template (diff of test.sh is empty; template task.toml lines 18/21/27 and template judge.toml timeouts 600/600/9000/900/900 match) and to staged-task-contract.md line 111 ('gates 1500, scored 11100, verifier 13200'). No timeout was changed, so no authorization record is needed. AGENT/BUILD: [agent] timeout_sec = 7200.0 and build_timeout_sec = 600.0 are the template values; environment/Dockerfile is node:22-bookworm-slim plus one apt layer and a global install of express and better-sqlite3 only, a realistic cold build well under 600 s. LONG ENOUGH (not measured on these bytes). Workload here is 1 + 2 gate criteria, 43 Functional criteria (37,295 characters of criterion text, one single-use restart), 6 Polish and 3 Visual. The only configured-judge timing is the hosted Oracle run on an EARLIER candidate (41 Functional criteria): result.json verifier started 10:10:47.88Z, finished 10:52:12.66Z = 2485 s for the whole verifier against a 12600 s combined budget, with the restart logged at 10:30:56Z, reward.json graded=1, exception_info null. That is about 20% of the budget and suggests ample headroom, but it is one run on different bytes; the logs carry no per-judge duration, so the 900 s Polish and 900 s Visual judges and the 600 s gate judges have no individual measurement, and no run exists for a weaker or slower submission (where a judge retries failing interactions and runs longer than on the golden). The scripted golden run is Playwright time, not judge time, and was not run through tests/test.sh. All 22 hashes in raw-evidence-index.json were recomputed and match. Verdict is Pass on the arithmetic and canonical values; risk stays true because the configured-judge workload on these exact bytes is unmeasured.
